lessons.title: Your first PivotTable
lessons.mac:
Insert > PivotTable works the same on Excel for Mac
Right-click = Control-click or two-finger tap
Fields pane closed? PivotTable Analyze > Field List

steps.say: Here's what we'll build. Two hundred and forty sales invoices for the year, summarised by region and product category in one small table, with a branch filter on top. Your manager asks for this every Monday, and a PivotTable builds it in under a minute.

acts.t:
Result: one PivotTable at N6 on sheet S12-01
Rows: Region  |  Columns: Category
Values: Sum of Sales  |  Filter: Branch
240 invoices become a 4 x 4 summary with totals

steps.say: In this lesson you'll create a PivotTable from a range, place fields in rows, columns, values and filters, and cross-check the total. Open the practice workbook and go to sheet S12-01.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Create a PivotTable from a range
• Rows, Columns, Values and Filters
• Cross-check the grand total
• Recommended PivotTables
Practice sheet: S12-01

steps.say: A PivotTable is a summary you build by ticking fields. Rows list items down the side, columns list items across the top, values are the numbers Excel adds up, and a filter lets you look at one slice at a time. It needs clean data: one header row and no blank rows.

acts.t:
PivotTable building blocks
Rows: items down the side (Region)
Columns: items across the top (Category)
Values: numbers to summarise (Sum of Sales)
Filters: one dropdown that filters the whole report
Source data: one header row, no blank rows or columns, one kind of data per column

steps.say: Here's our data: date, invoice number, region, branch, salesperson, category, product, quantity, rate, sales and cost. Click any cell in it, here A1. On the Insert tab, click PivotTable and choose From Table or Range.
Excel picks up the whole block, A1 to L241. Choose Existing Worksheet, and for Location type S12-01, exclamation mark, N6, so the pivot sits right next to the data. Click OK.
The PivotTable Fields pane opens on the right with every column heading as a field. Tick Region. Text fields go to Rows, so the four regions appear down the side.
Now tick Sales. Number fields go to Values, and Excel adds them up for each region. The heading says Sum of Sales.
Tick Category. It lands in Rows under Region, which makes a long list. In the Rows box, click Category and choose Move to Columns.
Now each region is a row and each category is a column. Every cell is the sales for that pair, and the bottom right cell, S12, is the grand total of all sales.
Tick Branch, click it in the Rows box and choose Move to Filters. A Branch dropdown appears above the pivot at N4. Use it when you want the same report for one branch.
Always cross-check a new pivot. Click N2, type equals SUM, open bracket, J2 colon J241, close bracket, and press Return. It matches the grand total in S12, so no invoice was missed.

Here's the most common mistake. If the source has a blank row, Excel stops the range at the blank and the pivot quietly misses everything below it. Your cross-check won't match. Delete blank rows, or turn the data into a Table first.

acts.t:
Common mistake: a blank row in the data
Excel's automatic range stops at the first blank row, so the pivot misses the rows below.
Fix: delete blank rows and headings in merged cells, then refresh
Better: convert the data to a Table with Command T before you insert the pivot

steps.say: When you're not sure where to start, select the data and go to Insert, Recommended PivotTables. Excel suggests a few ready layouts from your columns. Pick one and adjust the fields from there.

acts.t:
Pro tip: Recommended PivotTables
Insert > Recommended PivotTables (Excel for Mac and Windows)
In Excel for the web, the Insert PivotTable pane also lists suggested PivotTables
Pick one, then tick or untick fields to adjust

steps.say: On a Mac, the steps are the same: Insert, PivotTable. To right-click, use Control-click or a two-finger tap. If the fields pane disappears, click inside the pivot and choose Field List on the PivotTable Analyze tab.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Insert > PivotTable works the same on Excel for Mac
Right-click = Control-click or two-finger tap
Fields pane closed? PivotTable Analyze > Field List

steps.say: To recap. Start from clean data and insert the pivot where you can see it. Tick fields, then move them between rows, columns and filters. And always cross-check the grand total with a simple SUM.

acts.t:
Recap
• Click in clean data, then Insert > PivotTable > Existing Worksheet
• Text fields go to Rows, numbers to Values; move fields between areas from the area boxes
• Cross-check the grand total with a simple SUM

steps.say: Your turn. On the same pivot, show Salesperson in Rows and Sum of Qty in Values, then sort it largest first. Find the salesperson who sold the most units. The answer is on S12-01 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
On S12-01: Rows = Salesperson, Values = Sum of Qty
Sort largest to smallest
Who sold the most units?
Answer: S12-01 Done

lessons.title: Layout and design
lessons.mac:
Design and PivotTable Analyze tabs: same buttons as shown
Comma format: Control Shift 1
Right-click = Control-click > Number Format
Options: PivotTable Analyze > Options

steps.say: Here's the finished report. Region and branch in their own columns, every row labelled, no clutter of subtotals, and sales shown in lakhs and crores with the rupee sign. It looks like a report you can paste into an email, not a raw pivot.

acts.t:
Result: PivotTable at N6 on S12-02
Tabular Form, labels repeated, no subtotals, banded rows
Rows: Region, Branch
Values: Total Sales (₹ lakh/crore format), Sum of Cost

steps.say: You'll learn the three report layouts, how to repeat labels and remove subtotals, and how to apply a number format that survives every refresh. We're on sheet S12-02, recorded in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Compact, Outline and Tabular layouts
• Repeat labels, subtotals, grand totals
• Number formats that stick
• Rename value headings
Practice sheet: S12-02

steps.say: Excel has three layouts. Compact puts all row fields in one column. Outline and Tabular give each field its own column, and Tabular looks most like a normal table. These settings live on the Design tab.

acts.t:
Report layouts (Design > Report Layout)
Compact: all row fields in one column (default)
Outline: one column per field, subtotals on top
Tabular: one column per field, subtotals at the bottom, reads like a table
Also on Design: Subtotals, Grand Totals, Blank Rows, Banded Rows

steps.say: On sheet S12-02, click A1 inside the data. Go to Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, set the location to S12-02, exclamation mark, N6, and click OK.
Tick Region, Branch, Sales and Cost. Both text fields go to Rows, so each branch sits under its region, squeezed into one column. That's Compact form.
On the Design tab, click Report Layout and choose Show in Tabular Form. Region and Branch now get their own columns with proper headings.
Region names appear only once per group. That looks tidy, but it breaks when you copy the report or filter it. Click Report Layout again and choose Repeat All Item Labels.
We don't need a subtotal for every region here. Click Subtotals and choose Do Not Show Subtotals. The grand total stays at the bottom, in row fifteen.
Now the numbers, and a common mistake: formatting pivot cells like ordinary cells. Select the cost figures, Q7 to Q14, and press Control Shift 1 for a comma format.
It looks fine until the pivot changes. Untick Cost and tick it again, which is what happens when someone rearranges the report. The formatting is gone.
The right way is to format the field, not the cells. Right-click any sales figure, here P7, and choose Number Format.
In the Format Cells box, choose Custom and enter our Indian rupee format, which shows lakhs and crores with the rupee sign. Click OK. This format stays through refreshes and layout changes.
Headings like Sum of Sales look machine-made. Click P6, type Total Sales and press Return. You can't use the exact name of a source column, so plain Sales would be rejected.

acts.h: Type Total Sales and press Return

steps.say: A pro tip. On every refresh, Excel resizes the pivot columns and undoes your widths. On PivotTable Analyze, click Options, untick Autofit column widths on update, and click OK.
Finally, on the Design tab, tick Banded Rows so a long report is easier to read across the line.
On a Mac, the Design and PivotTable Analyze tabs have the same buttons. The number shortcut is Control Shift 1 there too, and Number Format is on the Control-click menu.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Design and PivotTable Analyze tabs: same buttons as shown
Comma format: Control Shift 1
Right-click = Control-click > Number Format
Options: PivotTable Analyze > Options

steps.say: To recap. Tabular form with repeated labels makes a pivot read like a normal table. Subtotals and grand totals are controlled from the Design tab. And always format the field through Number Format so it sticks.

acts.t:
Recap
• Tabular Form + Repeat All Item Labels makes a pivot read like a table
• Subtotals and Grand Totals are switched on and off from the Design tab
• Format the field with Number Format, not the cells, so it sticks

steps.say: Your turn. Switch the layout to Outline form, show subtotals at the top of each group, insert a blank line after each region, and give Sum of Cost the same rupee format. Compare with S12-02 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
On S12-02: Report Layout > Show in Outline Form
Subtotals at top of group, Blank Rows after each item
Format Sum of Cost with the rupee format
Answer: S12-02 Done

lessons.title: Summarise and Show Values As
learn: % of total, running total, rank, difference from last month

steps.say: By the end of this lesson our pivot will show how sales moved month by month: how much more or less we sold than the previous month. On the way we'll get counts, averages, shares of total and running totals from the same field, without one formula.

acts.t:
Result: PivotTable at N6 on S12-03
Rows: Month (2025-04 to 2026-03)
Values: Sum of Sales shown as Difference From the previous month
Also: Count, Average, Max, % of Grand Total, Running Total

steps.say: You'll learn the difference between Summarise Values By and Show Values As, and use percentage of total, running total and difference from last month. Practice sheet: S12-03.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Summarize Values By: Sum, Count, Average, Max
• Show Values As: % of Grand Total, Running Total In, Difference From
• Base field and base item
Practice sheet: S12-03

steps.say: Two settings, both on the right-click menu of a value. Summarise Values By decides how the numbers are combined. Show Values As decides how the result is presented, for example as a share of the total or a change from last month.

acts.t:
Summarize Values By: how numbers combine
Sum, Count, Average, Max, Min

Show Values As: how results are shown
% of Grand Total, % of Parent Row Total
Running Total In (base field)
Rank Largest to Smallest
Difference From (base field, base item)

steps.say: On sheet S12-03, click A1, then Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-03, exclamation mark, N6, and click OK.
Tick Salesperson and Sales. We get total sales for each of our sixteen salespeople, with the grand total at the bottom.
Right-click any sales value, here O7. Choose Summarize Values By, then Count. Now it shows how many invoices each person raised, and the heading changes to Count of Sales.
Same menu, choose Average. This is the average invoice value, useful when one person has many small orders and another has a few large ones.
Choose Max to see each person's single biggest invoice of the year.
Switch back to Sum before the next step, because Show Values As works on top of whatever summary you pick.
Now right-click, Show Values As, percentage of Grand Total. Each person's share of company sales, adding up to one hundred percent.
For trends we need months. Untick Salesperson and tick Month. Our Month column is written as year, dash, month, so it sorts in order from April to March.
Right-click a value, Show Values As, Running Total In. Choose Month as the base field and click OK. Each month now shows sales so far this financial year, and March equals the yearly total.
Last one. Show Values As, Difference From. Base field Month, base item previous. Click OK.
April is blank because there's no earlier month to compare. Negative numbers are months where sales fell. That's your month-on-month change, ready for the review meeting.

A common mistake: picking a base field that isn't in the pivot. Running Total and Difference From need the field that's actually in Rows or Columns. Choose Region here and every cell shows N A. Pick Month and it works.

acts.t:
Common mistake: wrong base field
Running Total In and Difference From need a base field that is in Rows or Columns
Base field = Region (not in the pivot) gives #N/A in every cell
Fix: choose the field shown in Rows, here Month

steps.say: Pro tip. You can drag Sales into the Values box a second time, so one column shows rupees and the next shows the percentage share. Then rename the headings to Sales and Share.

acts.t:
Pro tip: same field twice
Drag Sales into Values again to get Sum of Sales2
Set the second one to % of Grand Total
Rename headings: Sales, Share %

steps.say: To recap. Summarise Values By changes the maths. Show Values As changes how the result is shown. And running totals or differences need a base field that's in the pivot.

acts.t:
Recap
• Summarize Values By changes the maths: Sum, Count, Average, Max
• Show Values As changes the view: % of total, running total, difference
• Running Total and Difference From need a base field from Rows or Columns

steps.say: Your turn. Put Salesperson back in Rows and show Sum of Sales as Rank Largest to Smallest. Find who is ranked number one. The answer is on S12-03 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Rows = Salesperson, Values = Sum of Sales
Show Values As > Rank Largest to Smallest (base field Salesperson)
Who is rank 1?
Answer: S12-03 Done

lessons.title: Grouping dates, numbers and items
lessons.mac:
Group dates or numbers: Control-click > Group Field, or PivotTable Analyze > Group Field
Group items: select them > PivotTable Analyze > Group Selection
Fill down: Command D

steps.say: Here's what we'll build: sales by Indian financial year and quarter, where Q1 is April to June, not January to March. We'll also group invoice values into bands of one lakh and make a custom group of branches.

acts.t:
Result on S12-04
Helper columns M (FY) and N (FY Qtr) in the source
PivotTable at P6: Rows = FY, FY Qtr; Values = Sum of Sales
Also: date grouping, value bands of ₹1,00,000, custom group West Metro

steps.say: You'll learn the three kinds of grouping, why built-in date grouping doesn't match the April to March year, and the two helper formulas that fix it. Practice sheet: S12-04, recorded in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Group dates: Months, Quarters, Years
• Indian FY and FY quarter with helper columns
• Group numbers into bands
• Custom groups of items
Practice sheet: S12-04

steps.say: Excel groups dates by calendar year, so its Quarter 1 is January to March. For Indian reports we add two columns to the source: the financial year and the financial quarter. Numbers group into equal bands, and any items can be grouped by hand.

acts.t:
Grouping in PivotTables
Dates: Months, Quarters, Years (calendar, Qtr1 = Jan-Mar)
Numbers: Starting at, Ending at, By (band size)
Items: select items > Group

Indian FY (April-March): add helper columns FY and FY Qtr to the source

steps.say: Sheet S12-04 has sales from March 2025 to March 2026, so two financial years. Columns M and N are empty and yellow, ready for our helper formulas. Click M2.
Type this formula. It takes the year of the date, adds one if the month is April or later, and builds the label. So March 2025 becomes FY 2024-25, and April 2025 becomes FY 2025-26.
Fill it down to the last row. Select M2 to M261 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select M2:M261 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: In N2, the financial quarter. MOD of month minus four, with twelve, gives months since April: zero for April, eleven for March. Add one, divide by three and round up, and April to June becomes Q1.
Fill this down too: N2 to N261, Command D.

acts.h: Select N2:N261 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now click A1 and insert a PivotTable from the range. Excel includes the two new columns because they touch the data.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-04, exclamation mark, P6, and click OK.
Tick Date and Sales. Excel often groups dates by itself into years, quarters and months. If you see every single date instead, we'll group them ourselves.
Right-click any date in the pivot, here P7, and choose Group. Select Months, Quarters and Years, then click OK.
Look at the result. Years shows 2025 and 2026, and Qtr1 is January to March. That's the calendar year, not our April to March financial year, so this split is wrong for Indian reporting.
Untick Date. Tick FY and then FY Qtr. Now sales are grouped the way your finance team reports: FY 2024-25 has only Q4, and FY 2025-26 has all four quarters.
Next, invoice value bands. Untick FY and FY Qtr. In the Values box, click Sum of Sales and choose Move to Row Labels.
Tick Invoice No, then click it in the Rows box and choose Move to Values. Excel counts invoices for each sales amount.
Right-click any amount, choose Group, and set Starting at zero, Ending at six lakh, By one lakh. Click OK. Now you can see how many invoices fall in each one-lakh band.
Finally, a custom group. Untick Sales and tick Branch. Select Mumbai and Pune, cells P13 to P14, right-click and choose Group.
Excel creates Group1 and selects it. Type West Metro and press Return. You now have a new field, Branch2, that you can use like any other field.

acts.h: Type West Metro and press Return

steps.say: A common error: Excel says Cannot group that selection. It means the date column has a blank or a date stored as text. Fix the source column, refresh, and group again.

acts.t:
Common mistake: "Cannot group that selection"
Cause: a blank cell or a text date in the Date column
Fix: fill blanks, convert text dates (Data > Text to Columns), then PivotTable Analyze > Refresh
Also: you can't group a field while it's in Values

steps.say: Pro tip. Put your data in a Table before adding helper columns. The FY formulas then fill themselves for every new row, and the pivot picks them up on refresh.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Convert the source to a Table (Command T)
Helper formulas become calculated columns and fill automatically
New rows get FY and FY Qtr without copying formulas

steps.say: On a Mac, right-click a date and choose Group Field, or use the Group Field button on the PivotTable Analyze tab. Fill down is Command D.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Group dates or numbers: Control-click > Group Field, or PivotTable Analyze > Group Field
Group items: select them > PivotTable Analyze > Group Selection
Fill down: Command D

steps.say: To recap. Built-in date grouping follows the calendar year. For Indian reporting, add FY and FY quarter helper columns. And you can group numbers into bands and items into your own groups.

acts.t:
Recap
• Built-in date grouping is calendar based: Qtr1 = Jan-Mar
• Add FY and FY Qtr helper columns for April-March reporting
• Group numbers into bands and items into custom groups

steps.say: Your turn. Show FY 2025-26 only, with Branch in Rows and FY Qtr in Columns, so you get quarter-wise sales for each branch. The answer is on S12-04 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Filters = FY (choose FY2025-26)
Rows = Branch, Columns = FY Qtr, Values = Sum of Sales
Answer: S12-04 Done

lessons.title: Calculated fields and items
learn: When to calculate in the source instead
lessons.mac:
PivotTable Analyze > Fields, Items, & Sets > Calculated Field / Calculated Item
Same dialog: Name, Formula, Add, Delete

steps.say: Here's the result: a pivot of sales and cost by category, with a margin percentage worked out inside the pivot. The grand total margin is the true company margin, not an average of averages.

acts.t:
Result: PivotTable at O6 on S12-05
Rows: Category
Values: Sum of Sales, Sum of Cost, Margin % (calculated field)
Margin % = (Sales - Cost) / Sales, formatted 0.0%

steps.say: You'll learn to add a calculated field, why a percentage column in the source gives wrong totals, and how calculated items work and where they go wrong. Practice sheet: S12-05, in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Calculated Field: Margin % inside the pivot
• Why summing a % column fails
• Calculated Item and the double-count trap
• When to calculate in the source instead
Practice sheet: S12-05

steps.say: A calculated field is a new value field built from the totals of other fields. Because it works on totals, the margin is right at every level. A calculated item is a new item inside one field, like Laptops plus Printers.

acts.t:
Calculated Field: new value from other fields' totals
=(Sales-Cost)/Sales  -> correct % at every level

Calculated Item: new item inside one field
=Laptops+Printers  -> careful, adds to the grand total

Path: PivotTable Analyze > Fields, Items, & Sets

steps.say: Sheet S12-05 has one extra column, M, Line Margin percent, worked out for each invoice. Keep it in mind. Click A1 and choose Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-05, exclamation mark, O6, and click OK.
Tick Category, Sales and Cost. Four categories, with sales and cost for each.
Click inside the pivot, here O7. On the PivotTable Analyze tab, click Fields, Items and Sets, then Calculated Field.
Name it Margin percent. In Formula, type equals, open bracket, Sales minus Cost, close bracket, divided by Sales. Click Add, then OK.
A new column, Sum of Margin percent, appears. Excel works it out on the totals of each row, so the Laptops margin is total laptop profit divided by total laptop sales.
Right-click a margin value, R7, choose Number Format, pick Percentage with one decimal place, and click OK.
Now the trap. Tick Line Margin percent, the column worked out in the source. Excel adds up every invoice's percentage, so the numbers run into thousands of percent. Meaningless.
Switch it to Average. Better, but it's a simple average of invoices, so a small accessories order counts as much as a big laptop deal. Compare the grand totals: they don't match.
So the rule is simple. For ratios like margin, average price or achievement percent, use a calculated field. Untick Line Margin percent.
Now a calculated item. Click a category name, Laptops in O8, then Fields, Items and Sets, and choose Calculated Item.
Name it IT Hardware, and in Formula type equals Laptops plus Printers. Click Add, then OK.
IT Hardware appears as a fifth category. But look at the grand total. Laptops and Printers are now counted twice, so the total is inflated. That's the risk with calculated items.
Let's remove it. Click O8, open Calculated Item again, choose IT Hardware in the Name box, click Delete, then OK. The grand total is correct again.
When should you calculate in the source instead? When the result belongs to each row, like GST on an invoice line, when you need IF or lookup logic, or when several pivots need it.

acts.t:
Calculate in the source when
• the value belongs to each row (line GST, discount)
• you need IF, XLOOKUP or text logic
• several pivots or charts need it

Use a calculated field for ratios of totals: margin %, average price, achievement %

steps.say: On a Mac, the path is the same: PivotTable Analyze, Fields, Items and Sets, Calculated Field.

acts.t:
Mac corner
PivotTable Analyze > Fields, Items, & Sets > Calculated Field / Calculated Item
Same dialog: Name, Formula, Add, Delete

steps.say: To recap. Calculated fields work on totals, so ratios come out right. Don't sum or average a percentage column from the source. And calculated items add to the grand total, so use them carefully.

acts.t:
Recap
• Calculated fields work on totals, so ratios are right at every level
• Never sum or average a % column from the source
• Calculated items add to the grand total; use them with care

steps.say: Your turn. Add a calculated field called Profit, equal to Sales minus Cost, and give it the rupee format. Find the category that earns the most profit. The answer is on S12-05 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Calculated Field: Profit = Sales - Cost
Format with the rupee lakh/crore format
Which category earns the most profit?
Answer: S12-05 Done

lessons.title: Slicers, timelines and report connections
lessons.mac:
PivotTable Analyze > Insert Slicer / Insert Timeline
Slicer tab > Report Connections
Select several slicer items: Command-click

steps.say: Here's the finished sheet: two pivots, one with sales by branch and one with quantity by category, both controlled by a single region slicer and a single date timeline. One click updates the whole report.

acts.t:
Result on S12-06
PivotTable1 at N6: Branch, Sum of Sales
PivotTable2 at N20: Category, Sum of Qty
Region slicer + Date timeline, each connected to both pivots

steps.say: You'll learn to insert a slicer, connect it to more than one pivot, and filter by month with a timeline. Practice sheet: S12-06, recorded in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Insert Slicer
• Report Connections: one slicer, many pivots
• Insert Timeline for dates
Practice sheet: S12-06

steps.say: A slicer is a set of buttons that filters a pivot by one field. A timeline is a slider for dates. Report Connections links one slicer or timeline to every pivot built from the same data.

acts.t:
Slicer: buttons that filter by a field (Region)
Timeline: date slider by years, quarters, months or days
Report Connections: link one slicer to several pivots from the same source
Path: PivotTable Analyze > Insert Slicer / Insert Timeline

steps.say: On sheet S12-06, click A1, then Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-06, exclamation mark, N6, and click OK.
Tick Branch and Sales. Eight branches with their sales.
Click back in the data at A1 and insert a second PivotTable, this time at N20 on the same sheet.
Tick Category and Qty. The second pivot shows units sold by category.
Click inside the first pivot, N7. On PivotTable Analyze, click Insert Slicer, tick Region and click OK.
Click South on the slicer. The first pivot now shows only Bengaluru and Chennai. But the second pivot hasn't changed. It still shows units for every region.
That's the common mistake: a slicer only filters the pivot it was made from. With the slicer selected, go to the Slicer tab, click Report Connections, tick PivotTable2, and click OK.
Now both pivots follow the slicer. Click North, then South again, and watch both tables change together.
A quick check. Click N2 and type equals SUMIFS, open bracket, J2 colon J241 for sales, C2 colon C241 for region, and South in quotes. Press Return. It matches the pivot's grand total.
Timelines filter by dates. Click in the first pivot, then on PivotTable Analyze click Insert Timeline, tick Date and click OK.
Connect it the same way. On the Timeline tab, click Report Connections, tick PivotTable2 and click OK.
Click JUN on the timeline. Both pivots now show South region figures for June 2025 only. Drag across several months to select a range, or switch the timeline to quarters.
Pro tip. Right-click a slicer and open Slicer Settings to hide items with no data. Use the multi-select button to pick several regions, and the clear filter button to show everything again.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Slicer Settings > Hide items with no data
Multi-Select button: pick several items
Clear Filter button (funnel with a cross) resets
Slicer tab > Columns: lay buttons out side by side

steps.say: On a Mac, Insert Slicer and Insert Timeline are on the PivotTable Analyze tab, and Report Connections is on the Slicer tab. To pick several buttons, hold Command and click.

acts.t:
Mac corner
PivotTable Analyze > Insert Slicer / Insert Timeline
Slicer tab > Report Connections
Select several slicer items: Command-click

steps.say: To recap. Slicers and timelines make filtering one click. A new slicer only controls its own pivot until you set report connections. And a quick SUMIFS confirms the filtered numbers.

acts.t:
Recap
• Slicers and timelines filter pivots with one click
• A new slicer filters only its own pivot until you set Report Connections
• Cross-check a filtered pivot with SUMIFS

steps.say: Your turn. Add a Category slicer, connect it to both pivots, and find Laptops sales for the South region in June 2025. The answer is on S12-06 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Add a Category slicer connected to both pivots
Region = South, Timeline = June 2025, Category = Laptops
What are the sales?
Answer: S12-06 Done

lessons.title: PivotCharts
lessons.mac:
PivotTable Analyze > PivotChart
Or click in the pivot and choose a chart from Insert: it becomes a PivotChart
Field Buttons: PivotChart Analyze tab

steps.say: Here's the result: a line chart of monthly sales by region, built from a pivot, with a category slicer. Click Laptops and both the chart and the table switch to laptop sales. That's a chart your management review can play with.

acts.t:
Result on S12-07
PivotTable at N6: Rows = Month, Columns = Region, Values = Sum of Sales
PivotChart: Line, title 'Monthly Sales by Region, FY 2025-26', field buttons hidden
Category slicer drives both chart and pivot

steps.say: You'll learn to create a PivotChart, tidy it up, and make it interactive with a slicer. Practice sheet: S12-07, recorded in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Insert a PivotChart from a PivotTable
• Title and hidden field buttons
• Slicer that filters chart and table
Practice sheet: S12-07

steps.say: A PivotChart is a chart tied to a pivot. Rows become the horizontal axis, columns become the series. Change one and the other follows. Some chart types, like scatter and treemap, aren't allowed.

acts.t:
PivotChart = chart linked to a PivotTable
Rows -> Axis (categories)
Columns -> Legend (series)
Allowed: column, bar, line, area, pie, combo
Not allowed: scatter, bubble, stock, treemap, sunburst, histogram, box & whisker, waterfall, funnel, map

steps.say: On sheet S12-07, click A1 and choose Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-07, exclamation mark, N6, and click OK.
Tick Month, Sales and Region. Then click Region in the Rows box and choose Move to Column Labels. Months run down, regions across.
Click inside the pivot. On PivotTable Analyze, click PivotChart. Choose Line on the left and click OK. Trends over months read best as lines.
Each region is a line, with months along the bottom. The chart and the pivot are linked: filter or rearrange one and the other changes too.
Give it a clear title. On the Design tab, click Add Chart Element, Chart Title, Above Chart. Type Monthly Sales by Region, FY 2025-26, and press Return.

acts.h: Type Monthly Sales by Region, FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: The grey buttons on the chart take space and confuse readers. On PivotChart Analyze, click Field Buttons and choose Hide All.

A common mistake is choosing a chart type that PivotCharts don't support, like scatter or treemap. Excel refuses with a message. Use line, column, bar, area, pie or combo, or copy the values to a normal range first.

acts.t:
Common mistake: unsupported chart type
"You cannot use this chart type with a PivotChart report"
Scatter, bubble, stock, treemap, sunburst, histogram, waterfall, funnel, map
Fix: pick column, bar, line, area, pie or combo
Or copy the pivot as values and chart that range

steps.say: Now make it interactive. With the chart still selected, click Insert Slicer on PivotChart Analyze, tick Category and click OK.
Click Laptops. The chart and the pivot both switch to laptop sales. Click another category to compare.
Look at the pivot: the same filter applies, and the grand total in S20 is now laptop sales for the year.
Pro tip. For a review deck, move the chart to its own sheet with Move Chart, or copy it into PowerPoint. Paste it as a picture if the numbers shouldn't change later.

acts.t:
Pro tip
PivotChart Analyze > Move Chart: put the chart on its own sheet
Copy into PowerPoint: paste as picture to freeze the numbers
Keep the slicer next to the chart on a dashboard sheet

steps.say: On a Mac, use PivotChart on the PivotTable Analyze tab, or select the pivot and pick any chart from the Insert tab. A chart made from a pivot is a PivotChart automatically.

acts.t:
Mac corner
PivotTable Analyze > PivotChart
Or click in the pivot and choose a chart from Insert: it becomes a PivotChart
Field Buttons: PivotChart Analyze tab

steps.say: To recap. Create a PivotChart from inside the pivot. Add a clear title and hide the field buttons. And one slicer filters both the chart and the table.

acts.t:
Recap
• Create a PivotChart from inside the pivot: PivotTable Analyze > PivotChart
• Add a title and hide field buttons for a clean look
• One slicer filters both the chart and the pivot

steps.say: Your turn. Change the chart to clustered columns and set the slicer to Printers. Find the region that sold the most printers in October 2025. The answer is on S12-07 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Design > Change Chart Type > Clustered Column
Slicer: Printers
Which region sold the most printers in October 2025 (2025-10)?
Answer: S12-07 Done

lessons.title: Refresh, change source, drill down and GETPIVOTDATA
learn: Report Filter Pages: one sheet per region
lessons.mac:
PivotTable Analyze: Refresh, Change Data Source, Options > Show Report Filter Pages
Copy / paste: Command C / Command V
Drill down: double-click, or Control-click > Show Details

steps.say: Here's where we'll end up. March sales are added to the data, the pivot picks them up, a formula pulls Pune's total out of the pivot, and Excel makes one sheet per region at a click. This is month-end in most offices.

acts.t:
Result on S12-08
March 2026 rows added: A222:L241
PivotTable at N6 (Branch, Sum of Sales, Region filter) now reads A1:L241
N2: =GETPIVOTDATA("Sales",$N$6,"Branch","Pune")
Report Filter Pages: sheets East, North, South, West

steps.say: You'll learn why Refresh sometimes does nothing, how to change the source, how to see the invoices behind a number, how GETPIVOTDATA works, and how to make one sheet per region. Practice sheet: S12-08, in Excel desktop.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Refresh and Change Data Source
• Drill down with Show Details
• GETPIVOTDATA
• Show Report Filter Pages
Practice sheet: S12-08 (+ S12-08 NewMonth)

steps.say: Pivots don't update on their own. Refresh re-reads the source range. GETPIVOTDATA fetches one number from a pivot by name, so it stays right even when the layout moves.

acts.t:
GETPIVOTDATA(data_field, pivot_table, [field1, item1], ...)
data_field: the value field, in quotes ("Sales")
pivot_table: any cell in the pivot ($N$6)
field1, item1: which row to read ("Branch","Pune")

Refresh: re-reads the SAME range. New rows outside it are ignored.

steps.say: Sheet S12-08 has sales from April 2025 to February 2026. Click A1, then Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-08, exclamation mark, N6, and click OK.
Tick Branch and Sales. Note the grand total in O15: that's eleven months of sales.
March data has arrived. Go to sheet S12-08 NewMonth, select A2 to L21, the twenty March invoices without the header, and press Command C.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S12-08 NewMonth

steps.say: Back on S12-08, select A222, the first empty row below the data, and press Command V.
Click in the pivot, and on PivotTable Analyze, click Refresh.
Nothing changed. That's the common mistake. The pivot still reads A1 to L221, and Refresh only re-reads that same range. New rows below it are ignored.
Fix it with Change Data Source. On PivotTable Analyze, click Change Data Source. Set the range to A1 to L241 and click OK.
Now the grand total includes March. Next month you'd have to do this again, which is why the next tip matters.
Pro tip. Turn the source into a Table with Command T before building the pivot. A Table grows by itself, so Refresh is all you ever need. Refresh All on the Data tab updates every pivot in the file.

acts.t:
Pro tip: build pivots on a Table
Command T converts the range to a Table
New rows join the Table automatically
PivotTable Analyze > Refresh, or Data > Refresh All for every pivot

steps.say: To see which invoices make up a number, right-click it. Here, Pune's total in O14. Choose Show Details. Double-clicking the cell does the same.
Excel lists the Pune invoices on a new sheet. It's only a copy, so delete it when you're done. Let's go back to S12-08.
Now GETPIVOTDATA. Click N2 and type equals GETPIVOTDATA, open bracket, Sales in quotes, then dollar N dollar 6, any cell of the pivot.
Then the field and item to read: Branch in quotes, comma, Pune in quotes. Close the bracket and press Return. It returns Pune's sales, even if the pivot is rearranged later.

If you type equals and click a pivot cell, Excel writes GETPIVOTDATA for you, which is why such formulas don't change when copied down. To switch that off, open the Options dropdown on PivotTable Analyze and untick Generate GetPivotData.

acts.t:
Watch out: automatic GETPIVOTDATA
Typing = and clicking a pivot cell writes GETPIVOTDATA, not O14
Copying it down returns the same value in every row
Turn off: PivotTable Analyze > Options (dropdown) > Generate GetPivotData

steps.say: Last, one sheet per region. Tick Region, click it in the Rows box and choose Move to Report Filter. The Region filter appears at N4.
On PivotTable Analyze, open the Options dropdown and choose Show Report Filter Pages. Region is selected, so click OK.
Excel adds four sheets, East, North, South and West, each with the pivot filtered to that region. Every regional manager gets a page.
On a Mac, Refresh, Change Data Source and the Options dropdown are on the PivotTable Analyze tab. Copy and paste are Command C and Command V, and Show Details is on the Control-click menu.

acts.t:
Mac corner
PivotTable Analyze: Refresh, Change Data Source, Options > Show Report Filter Pages
Copy / paste: Command C / Command V
Drill down: double-click, or Control-click > Show Details

steps.say: To recap. Refresh only re-reads the same range, so use Change Data Source or, better, a Table. Show Details reveals the rows behind a number. And GETPIVOTDATA reads a pivot by name, while Report Filter Pages makes a sheet per region.

acts.t:
Recap
• Refresh re-reads the same range; use Change Data Source or a Table
• Show Details lists the rows behind any number
• GETPIVOTDATA reads a pivot by name; Report Filter Pages makes one sheet per item

steps.say: Your turn. In N3, use GETPIVOTDATA to return Chennai's sales. Then set the Region filter to South and see what happens to the Pune formula, and why. The answer is on S12-08 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
N3: GETPIVOTDATA for Branch = Chennai
Set the Region filter to South
What does the Pune formula in N2 show, and why?
Answer: S12-08 Done

lessons.title: Project: monthly MIS report
lessons.mac:
File > Save As > File Format: PDF
or File > Print > PDF > Save as PDF
First: Page Layout > Orientation > Landscape; Print Area > Set Print Area (P1:U15)

steps.say: This is the monthly MIS report most branch offices send on the first working day. Sales, collections and target achievement for every branch, filtered to one month with a slicer, and saved as a PDF to email.

acts.t:
Result on S12-09 (March 2026)
PivotTable at P6, Tabular Form: Branch, Sum of Sales, Sum of Collections
S:U next to it: Monthly Target (XLOOKUP), Achievement %, Collection %
Month slicer = 2026-03, then File > Export > Download as PDF

steps.say: Meet Ritika from the MD's office. Every month she builds this report by hand. We'll build it once so next month is just paste, refresh and click. Practice sheets: S12-09 and S12-09 Targets.

acts.t:
Project plan
1. PivotTable: Branch, Sales, Collections
2. Targets next to the pivot with XLOOKUP
3. Achievement % and Collection %
4. Month slicer
5. Export as PDF
Sheets: S12-09, S12-09 Targets

steps.say: The data on S12-09 is the full year of invoices, with one extra column, M, showing how much of each invoice has been collected.
The sheet S12-09 Targets has a monthly sales target for each of the eight branches.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S12-09 Targets

steps.say: Back on S12-09, click A1. On the Insert tab, click PivotTable and choose From Table or Range.
Choose Existing Worksheet, location S12-09, exclamation mark, P6, and click OK. The headings for our extra columns are already waiting in S6 to U6.
Tick Branch, Sales and Collections. Eight branches with sales and collections side by side.
On the Design tab, click Report Layout and choose Show in Tabular Form, so the first heading reads Branch.
Now the target for each branch. Click S7 and type equals XLOOKUP, open bracket, P7 comma. P7 is the branch name. Type it, don't click it, so Excel doesn't write GETPIVOTDATA.
Next, where to look: the branch list on the Targets sheet, A2 to A9, with dollar signs so it stays fixed.
Then what to return: the targets in B2 to B9. Close the bracket and press Return.

acts.h: Type 'S12-09 Targets'!$B$2:$B$9) and press Return

steps.say: Fill it down for all eight branches: select S7 to S14 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select S7:S14 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Achievement is sales divided by target. In T7 type equals Q7 divided by S7, press Return, and fill down to T14.

acts.h: Select T7:T14 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Collection percentage is collections divided by sales. In U7 type equals R7 divided by Q7, press Return, and fill down to U14.

acts.h: Select U7:U14 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: The total row. In S15 type equals SUM of S7 to S14. Then T15 is Q15 divided by S15.
And U15 is R15 divided by Q15, the company's collection percentage.
Look at achievement: around a thousand percent everywhere. That's the classic MIS mistake. The pivot has the whole year's sales, but the targets are monthly. We need to filter the pivot to one month.
Click inside the pivot, P7. On the PivotTable tab, click Insert Slicer, tick Month and click OK.
Click 2026-03 on the slicer. The pivot now shows March only, and achievement drops to realistic numbers. Branches below one hundred percent missed their target.
Check one number by hand. March total sales in Q15 divided by the total target in S15 gives the company achievement in T15. The formulas next to the pivot update with every slicer click.

Pro tip. Next month: paste the new invoices, refresh, and click the new month on the slicer. The side formulas stay valid because the branch list doesn't change. If branches can change, use GETPIVOTDATA instead of P7.

acts.t:
Pro tip: next month in three steps
1. Paste new rows (or keep the data in a Table)
2. PivotTable > Refresh
3. Click the new month on the slicer
If the branch list can change, read values with GETPIVOTDATA

steps.say: Now the PDF. Go to File, Export, and choose Download as PDF. Excel prepares the file and gives you a download button.
On Excel for Mac, use File, Save As, and pick PDF as the file format, or File, Print, then Save as PDF. Set landscape and the print area first.

acts.t:
Mac corner
File > Save As > File Format: PDF
or File > Print > PDF > Save as PDF
First: Page Layout > Orientation > Landscape; Print Area > Set Print Area (P1:U15)

steps.say: To recap. Use the pivot for the numbers and simple formulas beside it for targets and percentages. Compare like with like, so monthly targets need a month filter. And with a slicer and refresh, next month's MIS takes two minutes.

acts.t:
Recap
• Pivot for the numbers, formulas beside it for targets and percentages
• Compare like with like: monthly targets need a month filter
• Slicer + Refresh makes next month's MIS a two-minute job

steps.say: Your turn. Switch the slicer to February 2026 and list the branches that missed their target. The answer is on S12-09 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Slicer: 2026-02
Which branches are below 100% achievement?
Answer: S12-09 Done
